how: We read the website of every Kansas City wedding photographer listed on Lazo (98 listings, 80 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: portrait studios that mainly shoot families and seniors, a photographer currently booking only portrait sessions, a Joplin-based team that travels in, and a national chain's Kansas City landing page. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Most Kansas City weddings land in late spring and fall; is my date already a weekend you are holding, and how many weddings do you take a year?
Can I see a full gallery from a wedding at a venue like mine, including the reception in low light, not just the highlights?
What is included in the package I am looking at: hours, a second shooter, engagement session, and how long until the gallery arrives?

picks.name: Kendal Banks Photography
picks.blurb: Kendal Banks has photographed Kansas City weddings since 2023 and pitches to fun-loving couples who want to feel something when they look back, not just have pretty photos. Based in Lawrence, serving Kansas and destinations across the U.S.

picks.name: ATN Photography LLC
picks.blurb: Documentary wedding photography from Lee's Summit by ATN, who says he walks into a wedding like a kid at an amusement park and tells the story from within, as a guest would. Elizabeth, his wife, is part of the business, and the site is written in his own voice.

picks.name: epagaFOTO
picks.blurb: epagaFOTO is a Kansas City studio with three photographers, a photojournalistic philosophy and clean editing, describing its take on luxury as quiet and refined. Clients come to a dedicated space to pick custom-made products over a glass of wine, and the team travels.

picks.name: Mariam Saifan Photography
picks.blurb: Mariam Saifan shoots bright, colorful, light-filled weddings for easygoing couples, with more than 15 years of experience and a background in architectural engineering that she credits for her eye for light. Based in Kansas City, works Arizona, California, Florida and worldwide; the site says 2026 is nearly full and 2027 is open.

picks.name: Epic Photography
picks.blurb: Epic Photos + Films is a small Lee's Summit team that has documented weddings through photos and films for more than ten years, and promises energy, direction and expertise on the day. Covers Kansas City and all surrounding areas.

picks.name: BGstudios Photography
picks.blurb: Brandi of BGstudios in Kansas City focuses on the emotional connections of the day rather than checklists, with an editing style she describes as intentionally timeless and true to life. Photography and film, weddings and elopements, with collections laid out on the site.

picks.name: TJ Stansbury Photography
picks.blurb: Going on ten years of weddings, TJ Stansbury has been named one of the best wedding photographers in Kansas City by The Pitch, Zola, Wedding Rule Magazine and Wedding Pioneer. Photojournalistic documentation with timeless editing, available for U.S. and international weddings and elopements.

picks.name: Claire Ryser Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: Claire Ryser has photographed more than 300 weddings since 2007 and says she is recommended by venues and planning firms across the Midwest. A detail-oriented, high-energy Kansas City photographer whose images lean effortless, lighthearted and vibrant.

picks.name: Cassidy Drury Photography
picks.blurb: Refined, editorial imagery for elegant celebrations, made to endure for decades rather than follow a trend. Cassidy Drury is based in Kansas City, documents weddings throughout the Midwest, and keeps bookings limited.

picks.name: Oh! Snap! Photography
picks.blurb: Ailecia Ruscin of Oh Snap Photography has documented more than 350 weddings since 2010 across Kansas, Missouri and a dozen other states, for the hip and modern couple. Lawrence-based, LGBT friendly, with a photobooth and an investment page on the site.

picks.name: Nagel Portraits
picks.blurb: Mark and Katherine Nagel are both photographers who met in Boston and now shoot weddings together out of Overland Park. Pricing starts at $2,500 and they state that most clients end up around $4,000, which they lay out in full rather than making you ask.

picks.name: Amanda & Camera
picks.blurb: Amanda shot her first wedding in 2005 and opened for business in 2018; she has photographed more than 60 weddings since. Wedding packages in Lawrence start at $1,800 and include an in-person consultation, engagement session and online gallery with high-resolution files.
